title: Company Information
heading: Five decades of building at national scale
paragraphs: Saudi Arabian Trading & Construction Company was founded in 1975 in general contracting, landscaping, catering, and airport support. Its first construction contract — prefabricated schools in Hofuf — was delivered in the company's first years, and by the early 1980s SATCO was installing and maintaining baggage and boarding systems at King Khalid International Airport, where it has worked without interruption since.

Through the construction boom, SATCO grew in joint ventures with international firms. When the boom ended in 1985 and those partners left the Kingdom, SATCO acquired their assets and brought their people into its own divisions. That decision turned a trading and contracting company into an operating one, and it is the origin of the model SATCO still runs: build the asset, then operate it.

The model has been tested at scale. In 2012 SATCO took on the passenger boarding bridges at King Khalid International Airport under a build-transfer-operate concession — 43 bridges with ground power and pre-conditioned air, designed, installed, and operated by SATCO until 2026 — and long-term concessions of the same kind now run at Abha, Arar, and Tabuk airports. In 2019 NEOM appointed SATCO to design, finance, build, and operate a village for 10,000 residents; the village opened within three years, and SATCO ran it through 2025.

Today the group works across four sectors under one management — airport infrastructure and operations, construction, integrated operations and support services, and public–private partnerships, the last through SkyBridge — so that design, construction, financing, and long-term operations are planned together. It is classified at the highest level by the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing for construction, operations and maintenance, landscaping, and catering; holds a GACAR Part 151 airside license; and is certified to five ISO management standards. Fifty years on, SATCO remains privately owned and Saudi-owned.
